God demonstrates deep empathy for the people throughout this passage: (1) In 9:16, God tells Samuel 'I have seen my people because their cry has come to me,' responding directly to the people's distress. (2) God appoints a leader (Saul) specifically 'to save my people from the hand of the Philistines' (9:16), acting on behalf of the people's needs. (3) In Samuel's address to Israel (10:18-19), God reminds them: 'I brought Israel up from Egypt and delivered you from the hand of Egypt and from the hand of all the kingdoms that were oppressing you... I myself saved you from all your calamities and your distresses.' This demonstrates sustained divine care and empathy for the people as a whole. The narrative shows God responding to the collective needs and suffering of Israel, not merely managing leaders.
